title: Reordering the fixed-object coproduct bar
statement: Let $O$ be a small set, let $A,F,V$ be small ordinary categories [def-nagata-category] with object set $O$, and let $j:A\to A*_O F$ be the coproduct inclusion and $v:A\to V$ a functor, all fixing $O$ [lem-coef-fixed-object-scat-pushout-coproduct]. For $n\geq0$ set $B_n=(A*_O F)*_O A_1*_O\cdots*_O A_n*_O V$, where each $A_i$ is a labelled copy of $A$. Give $B_\bullet$ the augmented simplicial structure whose first face applies $j$ to the first $A$ factor, whose internal faces fold adjacent $A$ copies by the identity of $A$, whose last face applies $v$ to the last $A$ copy, whose degeneracies insert an unused copy of $A$, and whose augmentation maps all factors to the pushout $(A*_O F)\amalg_A V$. Then the coproduct braiding and associativity induce an isomorphism of augmented simplicial categories from $B_\bullet$ to the bar with terms $F*_O A_0*_O\cdots*_O A_n*_O V$, faces folding adjacent labelled copies and applying $v$ at the terminal face, degeneracies inserting unused labelled copies, and augmentation to $F*_O V$. The isomorphism is the identity on the $F$ and $V$ factors and shifts only the labels of the $A$ factors.

source.place: Sections 7.4–7.6 and Proposition 8.2, printed p.279: reordering factors in the ordinary coproduct bar and checking faces, degeneracies and augmentation.

proof.text: Work in the category $\mathcal C_O$ of small categories on $O$ and functors fixing $O$. The coproduct convention is precisely [def-galois-finite-coproduct]: a family of functors from its factors to a fixed target extends uniquely to a functor from their coproduct. Iterating this property shows that a functor out of a parenthesized finite coproduct is uniquely determined by its restriction to every factor: apply the binary property successively down the parentheses. In $B_n$ call the distinguished copy inside $A*_O F$ the factor $X_0$, and call the remaining displayed copies $X_k=A_k$ for $1\leq k\leq n$. Write $R_n=F*_O A_0*_O\cdots*_O A_n*_O V$. All the copies $X_k,A_k$ carry their specified identification with $A$.

source.place: Tag 002J, definition-coproduct: universal property, applied repeatedly to the finite list of factors.

proof.text: Define $\theta_n:B_n\to R_n$ by its restrictions: $F,V$ go identically to their named factors, and $X_k$ goes identically to $A_k$ for $0\leq k\leq n$. Define $\eta_n:R_n\to B_n$ by reversing those restrictions. The defining property in [def-galois-finite-coproduct] gives both functors. Each composite restricts to the identity on every factor, hence uniqueness gives $\eta_n\theta_n=1$ and $\theta_n\eta_n=1$. A coproduct braiding is the functor interchanging the two coprojections and an associativity map preserves each of the three coprojections. Therefore braiding the initial $A,F$ and reassociating has exactly the restrictions defining $\theta_n$ and equals it. This also fixes the comparison for any choice of parentheses, without a separate coherence theorem.

source.place: Tag 002J, definition-coproduct: construction and uniqueness for the two inverse maps.

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i<n$, compare $\theta_{n-1}d_i^B$ and $d_i^R\theta_n$ by their factor restrictions, using [def-galois-finite-coproduct]. Both fix $F,V$. On $X_k$ both are the identity of $A$ into target copy $A_k$ if $k\leq i$, and into $A_{k-1}$ if $k>i$. In particular $X_i,X_{i+1}$ both go to $A_i$. For $i=0$, the first face of $B$ sends $X_1$ by $j$ into the distinguished $X_0$ inside $A*_O F$ and preserves $X_0$; this is exactly that same rule. For $i=n$, both composites preserve the copies indexed $k<n$ and send $X_n$ into $V$ by $v$; both again fix $F,V$. Uniqueness therefore proves $\theta_{n-1}d_i^B=d_i^R\theta_n$ for every face, including the first and terminal faces when $n=1$.

source.place: Tag 002J, definition-coproduct: equality checked on each factor; explicit expansion of the bar comparison.

proof.text: For $n\geq0$ and $0\leq i\leq n$, the degeneracy of the original bar inserts an unused $A$ immediately after $X_i$ (after the whole initial factor when $i=0$). Thus $\theta_{n+1}s_i^B$ and $s_i^R\theta_n$ both fix $F,V$ and send $X_k$ identically into $A_k$ for $k\leq i$ and into $A_{k+1}$ for $k>i$. Target copy $A_{i+1}$ is unused. The universal property [def-galois-finite-coproduct] equates these functors. In degree zero this says both degeneracies preserve the distinguished copy as $A_0$ and skip $A_1$; no arrow is chosen in the unused factor.

source.place: Tag 002J, definition-coproduct: equality by restrictions; explicit degeneracy positions in degree zero and in general.

proof.text: Let $P=(A*_O F)\amalg_A V$. Apply [lem-coef-fixed-object-scat-pushout-coproduct], using the braiding $A*_O F\cong F*_O A$ with the restrictions of step 2. It gives an isomorphism $\theta_{-1}:P\to F*_O V$ whose composite with the structure map from $A*_O F$ fixes $F$ and sends $X_0$ by $v$ into $V$, and whose composite with the structure map from $V$ is its coprojection. Consequently $\theta_{-1}\varepsilon_n^B$ and $\varepsilon_n^R\theta_n$ both fix $F,V$ and send every $X_k$ to $V$ by $v$. By [def-galois-finite-coproduct] these are equal for every $n\geq0$, in particular at $n=0$. This checks the specified augmentation, rather than merely an isomorphism between its targets.

source.place: Tag 002J, definition-coproduct; augmentation target and structure maps supplied by the cited pushout-coproduct node.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], a morphism of simplicial objects is a family commuting with all order-preserving operators. Any order-preserving map factors through its ordered image as a surjection followed by an injection. Delete the missing image positions successively to express the injection by elementary faces; merge each repeated value successively to express the surjection by elementary degeneracies. Thus the equalities in steps 3 and 4 imply naturality for every operator by composition. Step 5 is compatibility with the augmentation, which by definition is a map to the constant simplicial object (Stacks Tag 018G). The inverse family is also natural: from $\theta_m u_B=u_R\theta_n$ multiply by $\eta_m$ on the left and $\eta_n$ on the right. The same calculation applies in degree $-1$. The two families compose to the identity in every degree by step 2 and the inverse isomorphism in step 5. This proves the claimed isomorphism of augmented simplicial categories, with the asserted restrictions on $F,V$ and the labelled $A$ factors.

source.place: Tag 016A, definition-simplicial-object, parts (1),(4); Tag 018G, definition-augmentation. The elementary ordinal factorization and inverse-naturality calculation are written out.

proof_origin.place: Tag 002J (definition-coproduct), expanded factor-by-factor; simplicial and augmented conventions in simplicial.tex Tags 016A and 018G. Dwyer–Kan Proposition 8.2 motivates this comparison but leaves the operators implicit.
